inventory/medusa/reservations#a batch cr.note: Real bug (module level), already reported upstream as medusajs/medusa#17436. ensureInventoryLevels checks each item of a createReservationItems batch against the level's available_quantity read before the batch (inventory-module.ts:183-185), then adds the batch's total: two reservations of 1 at a level stocked 1 with nothing reserved, no backorder, reserve 2. Confirmed on @medusajs/inventory@2.22.0's own code over in-memory storage. Workflows may confirm inventory first; the module's own check does not hold for a batch.

recheck.evidence: packages/modules/inventory/src is unchanged since the pin; on @medusajs/inventory@2.22.1 two reservations of 1 in one batch still reserve 2 of a level stocked 1, no backorder.

inventory/medusa/reservations#an update.note: Real bug, already reported upstream as medusajs/medusa#16488 (closed as stale; confirmed again on #17215). updateReservationItems_ with a new location_id and an unchanged quantity checks the new location for `data.quantity ? data.quantity - reservation.quantity : 0` = 0 more (inventory-module.ts:656-672), then adds the whole reservation there (:629-638): a reservation of 3 moved to a location stocked 0 reserves 3 of 0 without backorder. Confirmed on the original module code.

recheck.evidence: Unchanged source; on 2.22.1 moving a reservation of 3 to a location stocked 0 reserves 3 there (and the old location keeps its 3).

inventory/medusa/reservations#the reserv.note: Real bugs, two paths (path 1 already reported upstream as medusajs/medusa#17215, path 2 reported as #17506). (1) Moving a reservation: the old location's -quantity adjustment is computed (:617-628) but applied only to levels ensureInventoryLevels returned (:684-702), which are the new location's: the old level keeps the reservation's quantity forever. (2) restoreReservationItems_ on an id that is already live lists it again and adds its quantity again (:780-796, :1179-1229): reserved 4 for live reservations of 2. Both confirmed on the original module code; the search's run uses the restore path.

recheck.evidence: Unchanged source; on 2.22.1 both paths still happen: the moved reservation's old level keeps its quantity, and restoring a live reservation adds it again (reserved 4 for live reservations of 2).

inventory/saleor/allocations#the stock's.note: Real bug. deallocate_stock appends one Stock instance per allocation, each with quantity_allocated = F(...) - n (management.py:399-405), and saves them with Stock.objects.bulk_update (:449). For two order lines allocated on one stock (two lines of one variant), the list holds that stock twice; Django's bulk_update writes only the first of duplicate objects (its CASE WHEN on the pk), so Stock.quantity_allocated drops by the first line's amount only while both Allocation rows drop. allocate_stocks (:203-213) and _reduce_quantity_allocated_for_stocks (:509-516) aggregate per stock first; deallocate_stock does not. The repro runs Django's bulk_update with a duplicate object on SQLite.

recheck.upstream: saleor/saleor main@1771e1c (2026-10-23); latest tag 3.23.44 = the pin; Django 5.2.18 (the pinned ~=5.2.18)
recheck.evidence: saleor/warehouse/management.py is unchanged since the pin (models.py gained only two docstrings): deallocate_stock still appends one Stock instance per allocation with F("quantity_allocated") - n (:399-405) and saves them with one bulk_update (:449). The Django repro still loses the second line's decrement (3 allocated against 0 in the allocations).

inventory/saleor/allocations#a deallocat.note: The same mechanism as the stock's allocated count law: decrease_allocations for two lines on one stock lowers quantity_allocated by the first line's deallocation only.

recheck.evidence: The same unchanged lines (management.py:399-405, :449) and the same repro.

inventory/vendure/stockMovements#stock a.note: Real bug (with a caller that triggers it). createReleasesForOrderLines and createSalesForOrder free min(quantity, the line's Allocation records) (default-stock-location-strategy.ts:79-106), and Allocation records are never reduced, so a second release (or a release after a sale) of the same line frees the same stock again: stock 5, allocate 1, release 1, release 1 gives stockAllocated -1 (and allocations made before the level row exists are not counted, while later releases are). Confirmed on @vendure/core@2.3.4's own services over in-memory repositories. OrderModifier.cancelOrderByOrderLines guards with allocations + sales - releases (order-modifier.ts:305), but OrderModifier.updateOrderLineQuantity (order-modifier.ts:220-250) passes the line's new quantity to both createCancellationsForOrderLines and createReleasesForOrderLines with no such guard.

recheck.upstream: vendure-ecommerce/vendure master@aba3e9c (2026-10-23); @vendure/core 3.8.1 (latest); the rule mirrors 2.3.4 (the last 2.x)
recheck.evidence: Fixed as a symptom in 3.8.x: commit 92e4f356 (GHSA-8ghm-q833-cmgp, 2026-10-05, atomic stock level updates) makes updateStockAllocatedForLocation clamp stockAllocated at 0 after a negative change, with a warning (stock-level.service.ts:278-325). On 3.8.1 the repro's double release ends at 0, not -1. Still present in 2.3.4, the release the rule mirrors; the mechanism behind it is not fixed (next entry).

inventory/vendure/stockMovements#a line'.note: The same mechanism: the strategy reads the line's Allocation records and never what was already sold or released.

recheck.evidence: getLocationsBasedOnAllocations (default-stock-location-strategy.ts:142-173) still frees min(quantity, the line's Allocation records) with no account of earlier sales or releases, and OrderModifier.updateOrderLineQuantity (order-modifier.ts:228-258) still passes the line's new quantity to both createCancellationsForOrderLines and createReleasesForOrderLines unguarded. On 3.8.1: two lines allocate 1 each, line 0 is released twice, stockAllocated is 0 while line 1 still holds 1 (the clamp hides only the negative).

inventory/vendure/stockMovements#a sale.note: Original name of the restated law. Refuted by a sale before the stock level row exists: updateStockOnHandForLocation creates the row with stockOnHand -n, updateStockAllocatedForLocation finds no row and does nothing. The original does it; variants get their level when created, so the law was restated for an existing level.

approval/openzeppelin/Governor#a proposa.note: Original name. Refuted with an additional timelock proposer: it schedules the proposal's batch (same calls and salt, so the same operation id) on the TimelockController and an executor runs it while the proposal is Pending/Active/Canceled; GovernorTimelockControl's state() consults the timelock only for Queued. The original does this (reasoned from TimelockController.scheduleBatch/executeBatch and GovernorTimelockControl._queueOperations/_cancel); GovernorTimelockControl.sol:19-22 documents it as the risk of extra proposers, so the law was restated for the governor as the only proposer.

approval/openzeppelin/Governor#a cancele.note: Original name (restated with the first, by the same documented warning): GovernorTimelockControl._cancel cancels only an operation it queued (_timelockIds), so an operation another proposer scheduled for the same calls still runs after the proposer cancels a Pending proposal. Shown by replaying tlSchedule, propose, cancel, wait, tlExecute.

approval/kubernetes/csrConditions#a deni.note: the original allows it: /status sets a valid certificate before any approval, then /approval adds Denied (types.go:194 describes what signers do, not what the API server enforces); kept as stated, so it stays in the corpus as a false law the search must not prove

approval/gitea/reviews#two counted appro.note: A modelling error found while classifying the unknown laws (2026-10-24), fixed in the rule: DeleteReview restores the latest official review of the deleted review's reviewer (review.go:1040-1044, restoreLatestOfficialReview(ctx, r.IssueID, r.ReviewerID), read again at 829b49c), but the rule's `l2` was the latest row of the request's `doer`, so a delete could restore another reviewer's review. The assumption now ties a delete's doer to By[id]. The law stays unknown (it needs invariants over two rows of one reviewer); its verdict at 548c343 was unknown too.
